paper.title: DRIVE: Modeling Skills at the Reasoning and Interaction Levels for Web Agents under Continual Learning
paper.central_claim: DRIVE separates web-agent experience into natural-language reasoning skills and programmatic interaction skills, retrieves/invokes them by task-page scene, and refines each library from skill-level failure feedback; on five WebArena domains it reaches 52.8% average success, 7.3 pp above the skill-free baseline, and reasoning and interaction skills are claimed to give distinct, complementary benefits that keep growing with accumulated experience.

provenance.session_note: actual_model taken from the worker system prompt (Sonnet 5.5, claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]); no session id / receipt exposed to the worker, so null

materials.note: HTML text render read in full; figure images (Fig 1-5) are not in the text, so Fig 2 scaling values and Fig 3 bars are only known through the prose/captions

evidence.quote: Experiments across five WebArena domains show DRIVE attains an average task success rate of 52.8%, exceeding the skill-free baseline by 7.3 percentage points.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline claim and magnitude.

evidence.quote: The main limitation is therefore not simply the choice of representation, but the absence of a clear separation and coordination between reasoning knowledge and interaction knowledge.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap statement; asserted from prior-work description, not measured before the method.

evidence.quote: In most cases, however, the experience is reused as a single object, such as a memory entry or workflow.
evidence.support_explanation: Author characterisation of nearest neighbours AWM/CER/WebCoach/ExpSeek.

evidence.quote: SkillWeaver [ 16 ] synthesizes reusable web skills as APIs through exploration and practice
evidence.support_explanation: Closest executable-skill neighbour; only skill-induction baseline actually run.

evidence.quote: we prompt the language model to perform a counterfactual analysis of the error trace by asking whether the task could have been completed if the agent had preserved its high-level intent but followed a different interaction procedure
evidence.support_explanation: Failure-routing rule: LM judgement, not an executed counterfactual.

evidence.quote: The induced interaction skill and its associated scenario descriptor are then accumulated into a new interaction skill pool for the current round, rather than updating the main library immediately:
evidence.support_explanation: Candidate pool; library updated only at round end (selection stage).

evidence.quote: At each step, the agent applies a singleton activation policy within each skill level: it selects at most one reasoning skill and at most one interaction skill according to their compatibility with the current task-page scene.
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval/activation rule with empty-set fallback.

evidence.quote: For reasoning skills, no clear local error is usually available, so DRIVE mainly uses the final task outcome as a weak utility signal.
evidence.support_explanation: Selection signal for reasoning skills is weak; pruning relies on confounded success counts.

evidence.quote: DRIVE therefore does not rewrite a reasoning skill after a single failure. Instead, it manages reasoning skills through addition, merging, and deletion.
evidence.support_explanation: Different update operators per level (reasoning: add/merge/delete).

evidence.quote: A failed selector is demoted or removed. A working selector found in later traces is added to the set.
evidence.support_explanation: Interaction-skill patch rule (selector-level).

evidence.quote: We then use a within-website stratified split, assigning 30% of tasks to training and 70% to testing, while keeping the task-type coverage of both partitions as broad as possible.
evidence.support_explanation: Selection/test split: disjoint tasks but same sites and deliberately the same task types.

evidence.quote: all experiments, including DRIVE and the reproduced baselines, use GPT-4.1 as the backbone and are evaluated under the same environment configuration.
evidence.support_explanation: Same backbone for all methods; baselines reproduced by the authors.

evidence.quote: We limit the web agent to 20 environment steps per episode.
evidence.support_explanation: Step cap stated.

evidence.quote: Following the standard benchmark protocol, we use the automated functional-correctness evaluator and report success rate as the primary metric.
evidence.support_explanation: Outcome measured by WebArena execution-based evaluator.
DRIVE per-domain and average success (single value per cell, no spread).
Strongest baseline; numerically identical to the 'skill-free baseline' of Table 2.

evidence.quote: The baseline agent, devoid of any skill library, achieves an average success rate of 45.5%.
evidence.support_explanation: Skill-free baseline = 45.5% (equals AgentOccam row; whether DRIVE is built on AgentOccam is not stated).
Ablation rows: Succ.-Int +4.3, Fail.-Int +3.0, Fail.-Reas +2.3, full +7.3 (sum of parts 9.6 > full 7.3). Single run per cell; GitLab gain for Fail.-Reas only +1.2.

evidence.quote: As shown in Figure 3 (a), the LM-based module achieves 69.1% overall accuracy against human annotations.
evidence.support_explanation: Attribution validated against two annotators on 81 failed baseline trajectories (150-task subset).

evidence.quote: It correctly identifies 36 of 47 reasoning errors, corresponding to 76.6% recall, and 20 of 34 interaction errors, corresponding to 58.8% recall.
evidence.support_explanation: Per-class recall; 14 interaction errors mislabelled as reasoning. Precision not reported (derivable: 36/50 and 20/31).

evidence.quote:
LM attr. | 49.3 | +3.3
Random attr. | 46.7 | +0.7
Reversed attr. | 44.7 | -1.3
evidence.support_explanation: Routing control: human attribution +8.0, LM +3.3, random +0.7, reversed -1.3 on the 150-task subset (one run). Evidence that mis-partitioning hurts.

evidence.quote: Each configuration is evaluated three times under the same evaluation protocol, and we report the mean and standard deviation across runs.
evidence.support_explanation: Only the 100-task error-type analysis has repeated runs.

evidence.quote: Reasoning + Interaction skills | 52.3
evidence.support_explanation: Table 4 (100 sampled test tasks, 3 runs): no skill 42.3±3.06, reasoning-only 48.0±1.81, interaction-only 47.7±2.52, both 52.3±2.52; reasoning-only cuts reasoning errors (35.7->30.3), interaction-only cuts interaction errors (22.0->19.0). Subset differs from Table 2 (no-skill 42.3 vs 45.5).
Shopping only (N=137): +13.9% input tokens/task, +23.2% calls/task, -7.8% input tokens per success. Offline skill induction/maintenance cost not reported.
Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: baseline average 8.2 -> 12.5 (absolute gains 0.3-7.0 pp); only one other backbone and same sites.

evidence.quote: As the number of training trajectories increases from 42 to 251, both task success rate and interaction-skill invocation success improve across most WebArena domains
evidence.support_explanation: Retention-over-experience claim; the underlying values are in Fig 2 (not readable in text); 'moderate fluctuations remain'.

evidence.quote: During online deployment, invoking retrieved skills also produces skill-level feedback, especially information about why skill use fails under the current task and page context.
evidence.support_explanation: Ambiguity: whether feedback from test-time episodes updates the library before later test tasks is not stated.

evidence.quote: our experiments use a DOM-based benchmark and do not fully capture the visual complexity of real websites
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated scope limit.

evidence.quote: DRIVE depends on reliable failure attribution; incorrect attribution may update the wrong part of the skill library.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated limitation consistent with 69.1% accuracy.

evidence.quote: SteP relies on manually designed, website-specific workflows
evidence.support_explanation: Context for SteP baseline (36.4%).

signatures.object: Experience store of a prompted web agent (baseline: no skill library; control row equals AgentOccam 45.5%)
signatures.information: Training trajectories (30% of WebArena tasks per site), final success label y, per-skill execution logs (selector matches, URL/page-state change, exceptions). Test-task content is not supposed to be visible; test-time feedback use is unspecified (E027).
signatures.operation: LLM abstracts successful episodes into parameterised interaction skills (operation templates with ordered selector lists + scenario descriptor); LLM attributes each failed episode to interaction vs reasoning error and writes a recovery interaction skill or a reasoning skill <mistake pattern, correction, verification>; per-round local patching of selectors, pruning, and add/merge/delete of reasoning skills by smoothed utility.
signatures.output: Updated dual library K=(K^r,K^i) with descriptors.
signatures.conditions: Needs reliable failure attribution (69.1% vs humans) and DOM/selector-addressable pages; reasoning-skill quality inferred only from final outcome.
signatures.feedback: Interaction: local execution signals; reasoning: final task label as weak utility.
signatures.selection_rule: Pool K_new held until round end; BatchPatch/Prune for interaction skills (remove after repeated selector patches fail); utility rho=(S+lambda)/(N+2lambda), low-usage/overlap deletion for reasoning skills. Thresholds/lambda not given.
signatures.persistence: Library carried across evolution rounds n -> n+1; no versioning/expiry beyond prune.
signatures.later_use: Retrieved per step on later tasks via descriptors.
signatures.claimed_effect: +7.3 pp avg WebArena success (45.5->52.8); +4.3/+3.0/+2.3 per pathway in ablation.
signatures.failure_boundary: Wrong-library routing (reversed attribution -1.3 pp), retrieval precision as library grows, DOM-only benchmark (E028, E029).

signatures.object: Per-step skill retrieval and invocation inside the agent loop
signatures.information: Instruction q, observation o_t, URL/page context C_t, descriptors d_k=<U_k page context, W_k task semantics>.
signatures.operation: Structural filter on page-context match, then semantic ranking over descriptors, singleton activation (<=1 reasoning + <=1 interaction skill); reasoning skill injected as guidance, interaction skill instantiated with arguments and executed by trying stored selectors in order; fall back to primitive action generation if none compatible.
signatures.output: Action trace alpha and local outcome e per invocation, or a primitive action.
signatures.conditions: Descriptor match must fire; applicability check against current reasoning intent.
signatures.feedback: Execution log phi per invocation fed to next round.
signatures.selection_rule: Compatibility with task-page scene; empty-set fallback.
signatures.persistence: Invocation logs persisted as feedback set Phi_n.
signatures.claimed_effect: Fewer interaction errors (22.0->17.7%) and reasoning errors (35.7->30.0%) in Table 4; slightly fewer steps (9.3->9.1 on Shopping).
signatures.failure_boundary: Descriptor mismatch leads to non-invocation (not counted as skill failure); no UI-drift stress test.

gap.author_gap: Experience is stored as one object (reflection, workflow, program), so abstract forms lose page executability while concrete forms do not transfer across sites; reasoning and interaction knowledge are not separated or coordinated.
gap.checked_gap: A real, plausible limitation of single-object memories, but the premise that reasoning knowledge transfers across sites while interaction knowledge is page-bound is asserted rather than measured before the method; the paper's own evidence for separation is post-hoc (Table 4, Fig 3b). No experiment compares against a unified single-skill store or against the single-object memory neighbours (AWM, CER, WebCoach, ExpSeek); the only skill baseline is SkillWeaver reproduced at 29.7%.
lineage: ReAct-style prompted web agents / AgentOccam observation-action design -> AWM, CER (single memory entries/workflows) -> SkillWeaver, ALITA, CASCADE (executable skills as single procedural units) -> DRIVE (two representations plus failure-routed maintenance)

gap.residue: Whether the two-library separation (rather than any added skill/guidance context) is what yields the gain is untested; transfer across websites is untested.
gap.stakes: If separation is not the active ingredient, the design adds orchestration cost (+23% calls) and attribution risk for gains a unified store might match.
gap.method_response: Two representations with level-specific update operators, scenario descriptors for retrieval, counterfactual failure routing.
gap.remaining_gap: Cross-site transfer of reasoning skills; unified-store control; attribution accuracy of 69.1%; retrieval as the library grows; visual/multimodal pages.
unresolved: Nearest-neighbour source papers (AWM, CER, WebCoach, SkillWeaver) are not in the pinned input package; characterised only through the authors' own related-work text (author_report). Request to controller: pin them if neighbour-level gap checking is wanted for both seats.
Absence of AWM/CER baselines is not evidence that they would match DRIVE.

rs_pattern.reason: Operation actually executed: a resource (accumulated experience) is partitioned by a discriminating property (reasoning-level vs page-grounded interaction knowledge) and each part gets a different representation and update operator (selector patching vs add/merge/delete). Supporting: the stored skills are retrieved and injected/executed at inference with no parameter updates (frozen GPT-4.1).
rs_pattern.executes_pattern: partial: partition and per-partition treatment are implemented; the success-condition of empirically characterising the heterogeneity first, and showing uniform treatment collapses, is not.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: unproven: the paper shows the library helps and that mis-routing hurts, but not that separation beats a unified store or that the cross-site transferability/executability trade-off is closed (no cross-site test).

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Main-card success conditions: (1) heterogeneity characterised before treatment - unmet (asserted; only post-hoc Table 4); (2) partition load-bearing - partial (reversed attribution -1.3 pp; no unified-store arm); (3) two things treated as one are decoupled - met conceptually; (4) treatment derived from measured property - partial (operators differ by whether a local error signal exists); (5) binding stage targeted - plausible; (6) guarantee - none. Sub-card C04 is about compressing trained artifacts by magnitude/sensitivity criteria; DRIVE does not do that, so sub=null (the parent has no other sibling).

met: decoupling of reasoning vs interaction experience
failure_modes_present: no ablation isolating decomposition from added context capacity

matches.reason: The skill library is a heterogeneous resource split into two typed stores with tailored maintenance; fit is partial because the decisive load-bearing controls are missing.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: C03 (canonical conditioning schema taught upstream, or retrieved reference substrate as first-class input): DRIVE retrieves descriptor-matched skills at inference without updating weights, but the conditioning channel is not trained, no whole-category holdout, no longer-context/nearest-neighbour baseline -> C03 not selected.

unmet: cheaper conditioning baseline under equal budget

matches.reason: Needed only to account for inference-time conditioning on retrieved skills; not a claim of conditioning-based generalisation.

condition_checks.reason: Library built from the same five WebArena sites as the test tasks (precondition holds, but see F3).
Distilled interaction/reasoning knowledge from own runs injected later, gain reported against no library (45.5->52.8).
No comparison of distilled skills vs raw-trajectory memory.
42->251 training trajectories curve (Fig 2, values not in text); library size vs retrieval precision not reported.
No out-of-distribution/cross-site evaluation, so small-OOD-gain failure cannot be assessed.
Attribution reflector validated against humans (69.1%); outcome labels from the WebArena evaluator.
Gains on environments other than those the memory was built from are not isolated: test tasks come from the same sites and the same task types.
Main tables are single-run; only the 100-task error analysis has 3 runs.
Whether test-episode feedback updates the library before later test tasks (leak/propagation) is not stated; flawed skills could propagate (69.1% routing).
Interaction skills are programmatic procedures offered alongside primitive actions with fallback to primitive generation; the library fits in context via descriptor retrieval.
Small-model gains: Qwen2.5-7B improves 8.2->12.5 but stays low; tool/skill use by small models not analysed.

unassigned: Reasoning skills as retrieved corrective guidance with verification instructions: nearest card is agent_loop_context_control/C18 (post-action verification), but DRIVE injects pre-step guidance, not before/after-observation verification, so not matched.
revision_proposals: (single paper only, case-level, not a candidate_pattern) variant of C19: split the distilled store by representation (natural-language reasoning rules vs executable selector-set skills) with failure-type routing; needs a second independent paper before candidacy.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: partition a resource by a discriminating property and treat each partition differently. Domain: distil a persistent store from the agent's own runs and inject it into later tasks. DRIVE does both: the distilled store is split into reasoning vs interaction libraries with different update operators.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: C19 cards describe one tips/shortcut/tool store; DRIVE adds a counterfactual-LM failure router. RS success conditions (measured heterogeneity, uniform-treatment collapse) are not met; domain precondition 'same environments' is met by construction.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: express the task as conditioning at inference without weight updates. Domain K29: add a programmatic tool/skill library alongside GUI primitives. DRIVE retrieves reasoning guidance (context) and executable skills (actions) with primitive fallback.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: No trained conditioning channel; no cheaper conditioning baseline; K29's small-model failure mode only partially probed (one 7B run).

claims.text: DRIVE raises average WebArena success to 52.8%, +7.3 pp over the skill-free baseline and above SteP, Go-Browse and SkillWeaver.
claims.setting: GPT-4.1, 20-step cap, five WebArena domains, 70% held-out tasks (same sites/task types), baselines reproduced by authors
claims.selection_vs_test: skills induced from 30% training tasks; test tasks disjoint but same sites and templates; test-time feedback use unspecified
claims.result_denominator: avg 52.8 vs 45.5; per-domain cells single-run; test-task count not stated (Shopping N=137)
claims.counterevidence: No variance for Table 1/2; DRIVE-vs-baseline gap (7.3 pp) larger than the 3-run SD (2-3 pp) seen in Table 4 but that is another subset; unclear if DRIVE extends AgentOccam.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On held-out tasks of the same five sites, in one run, with GPT-4.1, the library improves success by 7.3 pp over the no-skill baseline.

claims.text: Reasoning and interaction skills give distinct, complementary benefits.
claims.setting: 100 sampled test tasks, 3 runs, GPT-4.1 classifier of failure types; Table 2 single-run ablation
claims.baseline_control: no-skill, reasoning-only, interaction-only, both (no unified-single-skill arm)
claims.counterevidence: No control that merges both knowledge types into one store; sub-additive ablation (sum of pathways 9.6 > 7.3); error taxonomy assigned post hoc by GPT-4.1 on the same trajectories; Table 4 subset baseline (42.3) differs from Table 2 baseline (45.5).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Each skill type improves success and shifts errors toward its own category on a 100-task subset; necessity of separation vs a unified store is untested.

claims.text: Routing failures to the right skill type matters.
claims.setting: 150 tasks (30/domain), 81 baseline failures, two human annotators
claims.baseline_control: no skill 46.0; human 54.0; LM 49.3; random 46.7; reversed 44.7
claims.selection_vs_test: unclear whether the 150 tasks overlap the training split
claims.counterevidence: LM accuracy 69.1%; no repeats/CIs; differences of 0.7-3.3 pp between arms are small.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Better attribution is associated with larger gains; human routing +8.0 pp is an upper-bound scenario, not an achieved result.

claims.counterevidence: 'moderate fluctuations remain at intermediate trajectory budgets'; Forum saturates early.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Qualitatively upward trend in most domains per authors; magnitude unverified from text.

claims.text: Added context overhead is offset by higher completion.
claims.setting: Shopping test set N=137 and a matched subset
claims.counterevidence: One domain only; offline induction/maintenance LLM cost not counted.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On Shopping, per-success input tokens fall 7.8% while calls rise 23%; total system cost unstated.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: WebArena functional-correctness execution results; skills induced from the same sites and task types as the test tasks and no unseen-site evaluation, so not 'transfer'.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In the authors' single-run WebArena experiments (GPT-4.1, 20-step cap, 70% held-out tasks from the same five sites and task types), adding LLM-induced dual-level skill libraries raised average success from 45.5% to 52.8%, and failure-type routing quality changed the gain on a 150-task subset; this is an author report, not our reproduction.
not_supported: Superiority of separating the two levels over a unified skill store
Statistical reliability of the main-table gap (no spread)
unresolved: Whether DRIVE is built on AgentOccam (baseline row equals the skill-free baseline)
Whether test-episode feedback updates the library during evaluation
Source of success labels y in training episodes
Number of test tasks per domain
assessment.retention_trace: before: no library (45.5%) -> proposed change: dual-level library -> selection data/rule: training split (30%) episodes, pooled candidates, patch/prune/merge by outcome signals -> persisted change: library K at round n+1 -> later tasks: disjoint test tasks on the same sites -> measured gain: +7.3 pp (single run). Retained improvement is partly shown (train-on-train, test-on-test split) but the scaling curve is unreadable and test-time updating is unspecified.

G.reason: Real, specific limitation (single-object experience loses executability or transferability) with named neighbours (AWM, CER, SkillWeaver) and stated residual; but the heterogeneity premise is asserted, no neighbour except SkillWeaver is run, and nearest-neighbour sources are not pinned locally.

M.reason: Operations, signals and per-level update rules are concrete and give distinguishing predictions (each skill type reduces its own error class; reversed routing hurts). Weak points: 'counterfactual' attribution is an LM judgement, reasoning-skill utility is confounded by interaction success.

X.reason: Induction, routing, retrieval (structural filter + descriptor match + singleton activation), fallback, patch/prune/merge are all specified with formulas. Unspecified: label source for y, thresholds/lambda, round schedule, whether test feedback updates the library, prompts.

E.measurement.reason: WebArena execution-based functional-correctness evaluator is trusted; failure-attribution reflector is validated against humans (69.1%). Deductions: 70% test subset with author-reproduced baselines, post-hoc GPT-4.1 error classifier unvalidated.

E.causality.reason: Ablations over three induction pathways and routing controls (random/reversed) support that skills and correct routing matter. The central 'separation' claim lacks a unified single-store arm and a matched-context/token control; sub-additive ablation unexplained; AWM/CER-style memory not compared.

E.holdout.reason: Task-disjoint 30/70 split, but both partitions share sites and deliberately the same task types; no unseen website, app or platform; test-time feedback use unspecified; E35/E28-type expectations unmet.

E.statistics.reason: 3-run mean±SD only for a 100-task error analysis; Table 1/2 and attribution subset are single runs; failure denominators and taxonomy are reported; no CIs or tests.

E.cost.reason: Same backbone, 20-step cap and tokens/calls/steps reported (Shopping); offline induction and maintenance cost, latency, and baselines' budgets not reported.

rationale: DRIVE 把 web agent 的历史经验拆成自然语言推理技能和可执行交互技能，并按失败类型路由更新。WebArena 五站平均 45.5→52.8（+7.3pp，GPT-4.1，20 步）；消融、失败归因（LM 69.1% vs 人工）和反向归因对照给出了较好的机制证据。主要弱点：测试任务与训练任务来自同站点同任务类型，没有跨站迁移；缺少‘统一技能库’对照，因此不能证明‘分离’本身是增益来源；主表单次运行无方差；测试期反馈是否更新技能库未说明。RS 原卡：primary=heterogeneous_decomposition（子卡 C04 为模型压缩，不适配→null），supporting=adapt_via_conditioning；领域卡：experience_memory_retrieval/C19（强）、planner_grounder_interface/K29（部分）。claim_support=scoped，evidence_level=online。
